verdict.rationale: Flagsmith has a native experimentation product: multivariate A/B/n flags, a managed event warehouse, and a built-in Bayesian statistics engine. Its MCP server and Admin API give agents programmatic access to flags and multivariate options, so experiment configurations are clearly readable by an agent. Reading experiment results programmatically is only implied by the general claim that anything in the dashboard can be done via the Admin API; the API's stated scope lists projects, environments, flags, segments and users, not experiment results. missing for 10: documented API/MCP endpoints for experiment results and statistics, agent-oriented result summaries or ship/rollback signals, independent or hands-on corroboration of agent access to results.

support.subject: As an AI agent, I can read experiment configurations and results programmatically to summarize outcomes and recommend ship/rollback decisions

citations.quote: Flagsmith Experimentation lets you run A/B tests end to end on the platform: serve variations of a feature with a multivariate flag, collect events from your application into a managed data warehouse, and read the results with a built-in Bayesian statistics engine.
Anything you can do in the Flagsmith dashboard, you can also do via the Admin API.
The Flagsmith MCP Server gives AI assistants and agents programmatic access to the Flagsmith Admin API through the Model Context Protocol
Your assistant can manage feature flags, segments, multivariate options, and release workflows on your behalf
